The Diagonal of a Map That Has One

Source: R/prox.R
map_diagonal.Rd

Returns the diagonal entries of \(D\) when the map is a Matrix diagonal object, and NULL when there is no map, when the map has another class, or when a diagonal entry is zero or missing.

Usage

map_diagonal(pen)

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object.

Value

A numeric vector of length nrow(pen@map), or NULL. A unit diagonal object (diag = "U") gives a vector of ones.

Details

A diagonal map rescales each coordinate on its own, so a separable penalty under a diagonal map stays separable. Standardization is such a map: penalizing a column divided by its own spread \(s_j\) is penalizing \(\rho(s_j\beta_j)\), so the scaling leaves the design unchanged and the sparsity of a block is kept. A general \(D\) mixes the coordinates and turns the problem into the generalized-lasso problem, which requires a different algorithm.

The map is recognized by its class, without inspecting its entries: a Matrix diagonal object stores \(q\) numbers, while testing a dense matrix for diagonality would cost \(q^2\) operations at every call. A base matrix that is diagonal in value therefore gives NULL. distrib_penalty(), scad_penalty() and mcp_penalty() convert a square map whose off-diagonal entries are all zero to a Matrix::Diagonal() when the penalty is built, so a separable, SCAD or MCP penalty built from such a base matrix has a proximal operator.

A zero on the diagonal also gives NULL, because the transport divides by the diagonal entries.

See also

has_prox(), penalty_prox(), spec_diag()
